items.title: Steve Buckingham, interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 25, 2019 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: They could all play jazz. Chet could play jazz.

ctx.x: When you went to do a session invariably you’re going to be playing music that you might not like. How do you adjust your attitude towards that.

You just have to be professional. You were hired guns and you were only as good as your last record that you were playing on. So it was very competitive. Everybody wanted to be a studio player and very few get through the keyhole. Especially back then. It’s not so that way — it’s almost a nonexistent art now because the way people make records they very seldom hire studio musicians. In Nashville they do but not like it used to be. It used to be literally three sessions, sometimes four sessions a day, six or seven…
When you were doing this work as a session musician, were you like eyeing the producer and soaking that in?

items.title: Buckingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2019
items.q: Although Chet Atkins knew everybody. He told me the best rhythm guitarist he ever heard was um — Homer and Jethro — Homer Hanes.

ctx.x: There’s some real gems on the thing and I was listening to the one, “Stompin’ at the Savoy” with the Benny Goodman Sextet. And I hadn’t looked at the personnel but I am hearing this chomp-chomp-chomp-chomp — and I go man, Freddie Green’s really going at it. And then I looked and it was Charlie Christian. And that surprised me I guess because I’m not sure I had heard Charlie Christian do that. I was more familiar with his soloing.

On the electric. But they could do — now I’ll tell you a funny story that Sweets told me, Sweets Edison. Of course Freddie Green was the guy on the archtop acoustic rhythm. Although Chet Atkins knew everybody. He told me the best rhythm guitarist he ever heard was um — Homer and Jethro — Homer Hanes. Remember Homer and Jethro? The guitar and mandolin kind of comedy duo? He said Homer Hanes was the best of the old archtop rhythm players. Freddie Green was second. And those guys, the action on their guitars was up…

did some things in the studio. And I talk about it in there. They’d never talked about it before but Mr. Hammond had told me. And in all my delving around and all the notes and tapes and everything I found all that stuff too. But yeah, not too bad to have Freddie Green and Charlie Christian playing, and Lester Young trading off with them. I know it’s, like I say, heavy stuff.
